claims.text: An optimal balance between configurational entropy and aluminum-induced lattice distortion controls phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Aluminum is the primary source of the phase-stability-relevant lattice distortion.
The proposed entropy–distortion balance suppresses deleterious phase separation and inhomogeneous precipitation.
A predominantly single-phase or coherently ordered structure simultaneously underpins high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
An equiatomic or near-equiatomic, homogenized Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy can provide the predominantly single-phase initial microstructure assumed by the experiment.
Aluminum content can be varied while holding the other compositional and processing parameters constant to provide a controlled comparison.
The extent of lattice distortion varies as a function of aluminum content.
The nature of chemical ordering or secondary-phase formation varies as a function of aluminum content.
High configurational entropy lowers the Gibbs free energy of the equiatomic alloy and suppresses phase decomposition.
Lattice strain caused by aluminum atomic-size mismatch promotes controlled, uniform ordering.
The interplay of configurational entropy and aluminum-induced lattice strain slows atomic diffusion.
Slower diffusion prevents nucleation of deleterious brittle secondary phases.
An optimal aluminum content will yield a stable, predominantly single-phase or uniformly ordered microstructure across a wide temperature range.
The optimal-aluminum alloy will have greater high-temperature strength and softening resistance than both aluminum-depleted and aluminum-rich variants.
The optimal-aluminum alloy will have better environmental resistance, radiation stability, and cryogenic toughness than both aluminum-depleted and aluminum-rich variants.
Off-optimal aluminum compositions will exhibit increased phase separation or brittle intermetallic formation.
Prior work establishes an off-optimal-aluminum Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni baseline with increased decomposition or heterogeneous precipitation under comparable thermal or irradiation conditions.
A lack of systematic correlation between aluminum-dependent distortion or ordering and performance, or equivalent phase stability and properties in off-optimal variants, would falsify the hypothesis.
